{{nihongo|'''Izuhara Hachimangū Shrine'''|厳原八幡宮神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tsushima]].

'''Izuhara Hachimangū Shrine''' (いづはらはちまんぐうじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Nakamura, Izuhara-chō, {{ill|Tsushima, Nagasaki|Q991032|qid=Q991032}}, {{ill|Nagasaki Prefecture|Q169376|qid=Q169376}}. It is a {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}} of {{ill|Tsushima Province|Q1054861|qid=Q1054861}}.

Its official name is "Hachimangū Shrine" (without "Izuhara"), but to distinguish it from other Hachimangū/Hachiman shrines it is also called "Izuhara Hachimangū." Climbing the stone steps, the haiden appears beyond the rōmon (in photos, the roof visible behind the haiden is the honden); the plaque on the rōmon also reads "Hachimangū Shrine."

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, on the return from {{ill|Three Han Campaign|ja|三韓征伐|ko|삼한 정벌|zh|三韩征伐|qid=Q11249435}}, {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} visited Shimizuyama on {{ill|Tsushima Island|Q52051|qid=Q52051}}, judged it to be a mountain where divine spirit dwells, set up a sacred rock boundary on the summit, placed a sacred mirror and offerings, and worshiped the heavenly and earthly deities. It is said this became the origin when in {{ill|677|Q30622|qid=Q30622}} ({{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}} 6), by imperial order, shrine buildings were erected at the foot of Shimizuyama and {{ill|Hachiman|ar|هاتشيمان|az|Haçiman|ca|Hachiman|de|Hachiman|el|Χατσίμαν|es|Hachiman|eu|Hachiman|fa|هاچیمان|fi|Hachiman|fr|Hachiman|hu|Hacsiman|id|Hachiman|it|Hachiman|ja|八幡神|ko|하치만 신|mni|ꯍꯆꯤꯃꯥꯟ|my|ဟချိမန်း|pl|Hachiman|pt|Hachiman|ru|Хатиман|simple|Hachiman|sl|Hačiman|sv|Hachiman|tok|jan sewi Kasiman|tr|Hachiman|uk|Хачіман|uz|Hachiman|vi|Hachiman|wuu|八幡神|zh|八幡神|qid=Q261637}} was enshrined<ref name="Kuroda">'Expanded Tsushima Island Gazette' (ed. Tsushima Education Association), issued Sept. 16, 1973, p.519. These origins follow old traditions; currently the shrine office distributes 'Brief Origin of Hachimangū Shrine.' For updated treatment, see Hisae Nagatome, 'Tsushima Kokushi' vol.1 (ancient section), relevant parts such as "Myojin-taisha of Shikinaisha".</ref>.

A copy of a ridge tag from {{ill|1476|Q6611|qid=Q6611}} ({{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} 8) says "this shrine is the original mausoleum of Otokoyama in this province and divine spirit protecting the nation for ten-thousand generations." There is a folk tradition that it is also related to origins of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|Q710098|qid=Q710098}}, center of Hachiman worship, but these folk accounts are not adopted in the currently edited/published 'Brief Origin of Hachimangū Shrine'<ref name="Kuroda" />.

On Tsushima there were Hachimangū in {{ill|Kamiagata district|Q10868208|qid=Q10868208}} and {{ill|Shimoagata district|Q10868678|qid=Q10868678}}; the former (now {{ill|Kaijin Shrine|Q11559099|qid=Q11559099}}) was called Kamitsu Hachimangū, and this shrine in Shimoagata was called Shimotsu Hachimangū. Around the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023}}, it came to be called Fuchū Hachimangū.

In {{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 4), this shrine was once renamed '''Watatsumi Shrine''' by identifying it with the Engishiki myojin-taisha "Watatsumi Shrine," but in {{ill|1890|Q7832|qid=Q7832}} (Meiji 23) it returned to the former Hachimangū name and became "Hachimangū Shrine," and today does not claim relation with Watatsumi Shrine<ref>Even as a Watatsumi candidate shrine, ritual continuity with Hachimangū is not present, so later denial may have been proper. Another candidate is {{ill|Otowatatsumi Shrine|Q134930328|qid=Q134930328}} (Kuwa, Izuhara-chō), which also currently does not claim Shikinaisha status.</ref>.

It was ranked {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} in {{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}} (Meiji 7), and promoted to {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}} in {{ill|1916|Q2087|qid=Q2087}} ({{ill|Taishō era|ar|فترة تايشو|br|Oadvezh Taishō|ca|Període Taishō|cs|Období Taišó|de|Taishō-Zeit|eo|Taiŝo-epoko|es|Era Taishō|et|Taishō ajastu|eu|Taishō aroa|fa|دوره تایشو|fi|Taishō-kausi|fr|Ère Taishō|he|תקופת טאישו|hi|ताइशो युग|hu|Taisó-kor|hy|Տայսյո|id|Zaman Taishō|it|Periodo Taishō|ja|大正|ko|다이쇼 시대|lt|Taišio laikotarpis|lv|Taišo periods|ml|തായ്ഷോ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Taishō|nl|Taishoperiode|no|Taishō-perioden|pl|Taishō (okres)|pt|Período Taishō|ro|Perioada Taishō|ru|Тайсё|sh|Taishō period|simple|Taishō era|sr|Таишо период|sv|Taishō|th|ยุคไทโช|tl|Panahong Taishō|tr|Taişo Dönemi|uk|Період Тайсьо|uz|Taishō davri|vi|Thời kỳ Đại Chính|zh|大正|zh_classical|大正 (年號)|zh_min_nan|Tāi-chèng|zh_yue|大正 (日本年號)|qid=Q329174}} 5).
